Free courses · 18 puzzles so far · about 90 minutes

Backend engineering from first request to production

Learn to design, build, test and operate a bookmark API. Start with a local request, then work through databases, identity, caching, Docker, Kubernetes and a release project.

Start learning Browse modules

Course outline

  • Build and test your first service3 puzzles

    Start with one request, one durable row and a test.

    1. What happens when a client sends a request? Follow one bookmark from a client to the process that owns it.
    2. Did the first write happen? Make a lost reply safe to retry.
    3. Can two clients prove the rule? Test a retry through the running service and read what survived.
    Check what you already know
  • Release and recover a first version2 puzzles

    Follow the same row through a release and a storage incident.

    1. Where does the data live during a release? Replace the running service while keeping its bookmark file.
    2. Alive, ready, or serving the wrong thing? Diagnose a storage failure and rehearse recovery.
    Check what you already know
  • API contracts and relational databases4 puzzles

    Validate inputs, model owners, commit related changes and paginate results.

    1. Can an old client read the new response? Define the shape and meaning of a request before changing it.
    2. Can a bookmark point to a missing owner? Model relationships and query accounts that have no saved rows.
    3. What if the service stops between two writes? Save the bookmark and the work it creates together.
    4. Why does the same page cost less to read? Inspect a query plan before and after adding an index.
    Check what you already know
  • Identity and changes over time4 puzzles

    Limit access by owner, expire sessions, refresh caches and migrate data.

    1. Whose bookmark may this request read? Trace identity from the caller to the storage query.
    2. Who vouched for the caller? Follow a session from an identity check to permission on one row.
    3. When does a reader see yesterday’s list? Predict the exact interval during which a saved response can be stale.
    4. Can two releases share one schema? Change the shape of stored data while an older reader is still running.
    Check what you already know
  • Docker, Kubernetes and production operations4 puzzles

    Package the service, replace a pod, measure performance and deliver your final project.

    1. What goes in a Docker image? Predict which files a replacement container can read and write.
    2. Who replaces a missing pod? Watch a local cluster restore a process and inspect what survives.
    3. Which users felt the slowdown? Compare request durations, failures and resource pressure.
    4. What evidence earns a release? Ship a change with tests, a recovery path and a capacity argument.
    Check what you already know
  • Concurrent edits1 puzzles

    A check at save time that detects a change since the client read a record.

    1. What does the second editor see? Follow two clients editing the same saved title.
    Check what you already know
